Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

guess verb and noun

also a guess, make a guess, guess right, guess wrong, at a guess, I’d guess, conjecture, rough guess, a rough guess

classical

Ter. Heaut. 62–63: ut conjiciō
Cic. Att. 14.21.1: cito conjēcī Lānuvī tē fuisse

conjiciō, conjicere, conjēcī, conjectum

verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive or a question · Conjugation on Wiktionary

guess, conjecture, work out

Literally “throw together”: to put two and two together. Ut conjiciō, at a guess (Ter. Heaut. 63).

Other words

  • conjectūra, conjectūrae f. — a guess, a conjecture

    noun, first declension · classical · Cic. Att. 14.22.1: nē nihil conjectūrā aberrem; M-O s.v. guess right, guess wrong · Declension on Wiktionary

    Conjectūram facere, to make a guess (Plaut., Ter., Cic.: Lewis & Short); conjectūrā assequī, to guess right, and conjectūrā aberrāre, to guess wrong (M-O).

  • dīvīnō, dīvīnāre, dīvīnāvī, dīvīnātum — foresee, guess (what is coming)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.8.2: nōn equidem hoc dīvīnāvī · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • hariolor, hariolārī — guess wildly; talk nonsense

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 202: sed ego hoc hariolor; M-O s.v. guess: make a wild guess · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx cōmica hōc sēnsū: Plaut., Ter.)

    Properly “prophesy” (Cic. Div. 1.132); “talk nonsense, be dreaming” in comedy (Lewis & Short).

  • īnfōrmāta cōgitātiō — a rough idea, a rough guess

    also used · modern · Traupman 107: rough guess, īnfōrmāta cōgitātiō

    Traupman’s phrase, “a thought sketched in outline”; Lewis & Short does not quote it. For a guess, conjectūra is the word.

Examples

  • annōs sexāgintā nātus es aut plūs eō, ut conjiciō

    you are sixty or more, I’d guessTer. Heaut. 62–63

  • sed cito conjēcī Lānuvī tē fuisse

    but I soon guessed that you had been at LanuviumCic. Att. 14.21.1

  • nōn equidem hoc dīvīnāvī sed aliquid tāle putāvī fore

    I certainly did not guess this, but I did think something of the kind would happenCic. Att. 16.8.2

See also probably, think, suppose.
